Child span sampling

Native Datadog tracing and DogStatsD operation metrics.

Where the flag is set

Standalone binary

-sample-child-spans is read at startup. Defaults to on with native Datadog telemetry unless single-span sampling rules are configured.

Go app using the Datadog helper

Opt in at startup with datadog.Options.SampleChildSpans.

Go app with its own tracer

For runtime control, bump the library and wire the host app’s flag into its tracer as a follow-up.

Sample child spans for this query or batch?

OFFFull phase tracing

Create every phase span

Message handling, forwarding, execution, and returning rows.

Existing APM metrics cover those spans

With client-side APM stats enabled, dropped traces still contribute to phase counts, errors, and latency.

ONSample phase spans

DogStatsD covers every completed phase

Hits, errors, and latency by operation. Errors identify PostgreSQL or the proxy as the source.

Local root rejected at start

Skip phase spans. Child APM metrics miss this traffic, and a trace kept later can lack the phase details.

Kept, undecided, or propagated root

Create phase spans and retain their APM metrics.

Dropped traceThe sampler discards the individual query or batch’s span timeline from APM.

DogStatsD dimensionsThe phase metrics omit APM resource and peer dimensions. The latency distribution combines successful and failed phases.
